clue.text: Hair preparation doctor uses after treatment

indicators.note: letters that have been through a treatment come out processed and rearranged

blocks.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a standard crossword doctor
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A hairdresser recommends a styling product to use once the hair has been treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses after' reads as 'applies after', but the doctor comes first and the treated word follows him.
explanation.definitionFit: A styling foam combed into hair to give it body and hold is a common grooming product.

clue.text: Work round unpleasant matter

blocks.note: O is round in shape
the yellowish fluid from an infected wound

explanation.surface: Someone is working through a nasty, messy job.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a work, used especially of a numbered musical composition or a major artistic creation.

clue.text: Worried monster company, in short, shown at wind up time?

definitions.note: a description of when the thing is displayed, standing in for the noun

indicators.note: something worried is disturbed and agitated, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is the short form of company

explanation.surface: An anxious business giant is exposed just as the clock is being wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up time' suggests winding a clock, but it means the time when the wind gets up, a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas cone hoisted at coastguard stations and harbours as a warning that a gale is on its way.

clue.text: English man disregarding books? It's to show clearly

indicators.note: to disregard something is to leave it out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
any man's name will do; here Vincent
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An Englishman who ignores reading insists his point is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' stands for a first name; Vincent with the New Testament removed leaves VINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling or quality is to display or reveal it plainly, a formal verb.

clue.text: Bright colour-sergeant, say, in the dance

blocks.note: flame is a bright orange-red colour
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier in a vivid red uniform is spotted on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'colour-sergeant' look like a single army rank, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate Spanish dance of Andalusian gypsy origin with stamping heels and guitar accompaniment.

clue.text: Find difficulty in living in autumn on CD work

blocks.note: fall is the American word for autumn
taken as written
Hard Times is a novel by Charles Dickens, whose initials are CD

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to make a living from compact-disc work in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: CD looks like a compact disc, but here it is Charles Dickens, and his work is a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet with poverty or misfortune after being better off, so that getting by becomes a struggle.

clue.text: A fellow's good at speaking, having plenty of brass

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
able to speak easily and smoothly

explanation.surface: A smooth talker who is also loaded with money.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for money, not the metal or the musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people are rich, and brass in northern English slang means cash.

clue.text: Making it go round Eastern monarch

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: An Oriental ruler is on a tour, travelling round his realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' here means stretch far enough to serve everyone, as in eking out supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Eking out scarce food or money means stretching it so that there is enough for everyone.

clue.text: Only cheer leader of team excitedly in an orderly way

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, so only the first is kept
acting excitedly means jumping about wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the opening letter of team

explanation.surface: A lone cheerleader whips up the team's supporters with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheer leader' looks like one word for a pom-pom waver, but 'leader of team' takes just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking or acting logically and consistently, with every part clearly connected, is doing things neatly and in order.

clue.text: Discipline one lout with art lesson in small group

indicators.note: to discipline something is to put it in order, so these letters are reorganised

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher has to bring a single unruly youth into line in an art class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discipline' reads as a teacher's command, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A university teaching session in which a tutor works with one student or a handful at once.

clue.text: Part of arrow left in battle

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: a fight is a battle
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An arrow fragment is found lying on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The feathers or vanes at the tail of an arrow or dart that keep it stable as it travels.

clue.text: Small cuts to be made in this theatrical performance?

definitions.text: Small cuts to be made in this theatrical performance?

blocks.clueFragment: Small cuts to be made in this theatrical performance?
blocks.note: surface reading: a director trimming a few lines from a stage play

blocks.clueFragment: Small cuts to be made in this theatrical performance?
blocks.note: setter's reading: tiny incisions made by a surgeon in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A stage show is being trimmed slightly before opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is an operating theatre, and the cuts are a surgeon's very fine incisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate surgery on tiny structures such as nerves and blood vessels, performed under a magnifying microscope.

clue.text: Express link

blocks.note: first meaning: put into clear words
second meaning: join by a flexible joint

explanation.walkthrough: 'Express link' looks like a fast rail connection; the two words are separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to state thoughts clearly in speech and to connect parts with movable joints.

clue.text: Dash! Biro's broken

indicators.note: something broken falls apart and its letters can be put back in another order

blocks.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a British trade name

explanation.surface: An exasperated writer finds the ballpoint pen has packed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash!' is a mild curse, but it is the definition, meaning verve.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash here means spirited energy and flair, which is exactly what the Italian-derived word denotes.

clue.text: Dealing with Heather by writing

blocks.note: a person's hand is their handwriting
ling is common heather, the moorland plant

explanation.surface: Someone is coping with a woman called Heather through correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name but is the plant; 'by' means placed next to, with writing first.
explanation.definitionFit: Handling a problem or a customer means managing it, taking charge of it and sorting it out.

clue.text: The painting comes down to a head

blocks.note: an aircraft comes down when it lands
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: An artwork falls off the wall and strikes someone on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes down to' suggests something reaching its essence, but the head is a coastal headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture of countryside scenery is a common genre of painting, as hung in galleries.

clue.text: Salad dressing and no French wine for the bird

indicators.note: having the dressing with none of something means that part is taken away

blocks.note: oil and vinegar dressing
vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: A picnic order: dressing on the salad, but no wine, and something for the parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: Vinaigrette conveniently begins with the French for wine, which is struck off.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the egret, a white heron, and also for its plume of feathers.

clue.text: Relatively active part of body takes in rest

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it inside yourself

blocks.note: the liver is an organ of the body
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: An organ of the body recovers by taking some rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' signals the comparative form: more active than something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of lively, meaning full of more energy and movement than before or than another.

clue.text: Some feeling returns in the water

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, a run of consecutive letters inside it
something that returns goes back the way it came, so it is read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters in the middle of feeling

explanation.surface: Sensation comes back to someone once they are in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the water' is a river here, as crosswords often use water for a named river.
explanation.definitionFit: The great African river flowing north through Egypt to the Mediterranean is a body of water.

clue.text: Can spin or twist

indicators.note: twisting something bends it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice of dance moves: you can spin or you can twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb 'is able to', but it is the noun, slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is informal American slang for a jail where offenders are locked up.

clue.text: Copper darts start possibly to be thrown in farce?

definitions.note: a description of the things, standing in for the noun

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of these letters

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman's darts match is about to start, possibly descending into farce.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman but gives the chemical symbol; in slapstick comedy custard pies are hurled in faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry cases filled with egg custard are the classic missiles of slapstick comedy routines on stage and screen.

clue.text: Tug made from wood round the West

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it on all sides

blocks.note: teak is a hardwood
W is the abbreviation for West

explanation.surface: A tugboat built of timber sails around the western coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Tug looks like a boat built of wood, but it is a verb: a small sharp pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a quick sharp pull or twist, as on someone's ear or nose.

clue.text: Artist in middle of Poly examination

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, without the ends
one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: the central pair of letters of Poly
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An art student sits a test at the polytechnic.
explanation.walkthrough: A Poly was a British polytechnic college, which fits the exam surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a viva or language exam, is an oral.

clue.text: Temporary dwelling by the city is hidden from view

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: A camp beside the city is tucked away out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means next to; the city comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present but not yet showing itself, like a dormant talent or infection, is concealed.

clue.text: Make a killing in the service area

blocks.note: Mass is a church service
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: Someone earns a fortune in a motorway service station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a killing' usually means profit hugely; here it is literal slaughter. A service area is a British motorway rest stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to slaughter many people at once, a literal reading of the profit idiom.

clue.text: Don't break up so much, they say. It's careless

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: to break up is to wreck, and not so much is less

explanation.surface: Advice to a clumsy person: stop smashing things, it's sloppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without thought for danger or consequences is heedless behaviour.

clue.text: Dislike injection?

blocks.note: first meaning: hostility or antagonism
second meaning: the sharp instrument used to give a jab

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it sound like asking about a fear of jabs. In British usage needle is also ill feeling between rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for antagonism between rivals and also informal for a hypodermic jab.
